- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is positive (especially >0.36) — model tends to overshoot upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is weak or negative (sentiment <0.18) — model fails to capture downward risk or mean reversion.
- Forecast tends to lag true price movements by 1–3 days; adjust for recent sentiment spikes by adding 0.5–1.5 points to forecast if sentiment >0.36.
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment swings — if sentiment rises sharply, don’t assume price will continue rising; cap upward forecasts at +2.5% above recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment is low and price is rising, model often underestimates the continuation — add 0.5–1.0 point to forecast if sentiment <0.18 and price > previous 3-day high.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >+3.0 above recent 14-day average, reduce by 0.5–1.0 point unless sentiment is strong and rising.
- Don’t forecast price spikes if sentiment is weak — if sentiment <0.18 for 3+ consecutive days, cap forecast at 1.5–2.0 points below recent 7-day high.
